# The ecliptic and the zodiac

A red flashlight keeps night vision intact while reading charts at the eyepiece. A planisphere rotates to show which constellations are above the horizon at a given time. Right ascension is measured in hours along the celestial equator, and declination in degrees north or south of it. An armillary sphere models the sky with rings for the equator, the ecliptic and the meridian.

## Steps

- Averted vision helps: looking slightly to the side of a faint object uses the more sensitive part of the retina.
- The Perseid meteor shower peaks in August and often shows dozens of meteors per hour.
- The ecliptic is tilted about 23.4 degrees to the celestial equator because of the tilt of the Earth.
- An armillary sphere models the sky with rings for the equator, the ecliptic and the meridian.
- Saturn rings tilt over a fifteen year cycle, so their appearance slowly changes from year to year.
